title: Rethinking API Manufacturing with Biocatalysis
body_markdown:
One of the most significant developments in pharma biocatalysis is the ability to combine multiple enzymes within integrated reaction systems. Rather than performing each transformation independently and isolating each intermediate, multi-enzyme cascades can enable several transformations to occur sequentially within the same process stream. Integrated enzymatic cascades offer:


- **Fewer intermediate handling steps:** Integrated cascades can reduce repeated isolations, workups and purification stages, helping simplify the overall process.
- **Reduced reliance on organic solvents:** Enzymatic transformations can often be performed under aqueous or comparatively mild conditions, creating opportunities to improve the environmental profile of a route.
- **Greater process integration:** Linking enzymatic reactions can build molecular complexity within a more streamlined process rather than through a long sequence of discrete operations.
- **New synthetic possibilities:** Highly selective enzymatic transformations can be combined in ways that may be difficult to achieve through conventional chemistry alone.


Enzymes have to work reliably under manufacturing conditions and alongside other enzymes in the process. Their activity, selectivity and stability must support the performance of the overall pathway. Protein engineering makes this possible by tailoring enzymes to meet the specific needs of an industrial process.
